{{short description|Summability method used in harmonic analysis}}
The '''Bochner–Riesz mean''' is a [[summability method]] often used in [[harmonic analysis]] when considering convergence of [[Fourier series]] and [[Fourier inversion theorem|Fourier integrals]]. It was introduced by [[Salomon Bochner]] as a modification of the [[Riesz mean]].

==Definition==
Define

:<math>(\xi)_+ = \begin{cases} \xi, & \mbox{if }  \xi > 0  \\ 0,  & \mbox{otherwise}. \end{cases}</math>

Let <math>f</math> be a [[periodic function]], thought of as being on the [[n-torus]], <math>\mathbb{T}^n</math>, and having Fourier coefficients <math>\hat{f}(k)</math> for <math>k \in \mathbb{Z}^n</math>.  Then the Bochner–Riesz means of complex order <math>\delta</math>, <math>B_R^\delta f</math> of (where <math>R > 0</math> and <math>\mbox{Re}(\delta) > 0</math>) are defined as

:<math>B_R^\delta f(\theta) = \underset{|k| \leq R}{\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^n}} \left( 1- \frac{|k|^2}{R^2} \right)_+^\delta \hat{f}(k) e^{2 \pi i k \cdot \theta}.</math>

Analogously, for a function <math>f</math> on <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> with Fourier transform <math>\hat{f}(\xi)</math>, the Bochner–Riesz means of complex order <math>\delta</math>, <math>S_R^\delta f</math> (where <math>R > 0</math> and <math>\mbox{Re}(\delta) > 0</math>) are defined as

:<math>S_R^\delta f(x) = \int_{|\xi| \leq R} \left(1 - \frac{|\xi|^2}{R^2} \right)_+^\delta \hat{f}(\xi) e^{2 \pi i x \cdot \xi}\,d\xi.</math>

==Application to convolution operators==
For <math>\delta > 0</math> and <math>n=1</math>,  <math>S_R^\delta</math> and <math>B_R^\delta</math> may be written as [[convolution]] operators, where the convolution kernel is an [[mollifier|approximate identity]].  As such, in these cases, considering the [[almost everywhere convergence]] of Bochner–Riesz means for functions in <math>L^p</math> spaces is much simpler than the problem of "regular" almost everywhere convergence of Fourier series/integrals (corresponding to <math>\delta = 0</math>). 

In higher dimensions, the convolution kernels become "worse behaved": specifically, for 

:<math>\delta \leq \tfrac{n-1}{2}</math>

the kernel is no longer integrable. Here, establishing almost everywhere convergence becomes correspondingly more difficult.

==Bochner–Riesz conjecture==
Another question is that of for which <math>\delta</math> and which <math>p</math> the Bochner–Riesz means of an <math>L^p</math> function [[converge in norm]].  This issue is of fundamental importance for <math>n \geq 2</math>, since regular spherical norm convergence (again corresponding to <math>\delta = 0</math>) fails in <math>L^p</math> when <math>p \neq 2</math>.  This was shown in a paper of 1971 by [[Charles Fefferman]].<ref>{{Cite journal |first=Charles |last=Fefferman |title=The multiplier problem for the ball |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=94 |issue=2 |year=1971 |pages=330–336 |doi=10.2307/1970864 |jstor=1970864 }}</ref> 

By a transference result, the <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> and <math>\mathbb{T}^n</math> problems are equivalent to one another, and as such, by an argument using the [[uniform boundedness principle]], for any particular <math>p \in (1, \infty)</math>, <math>L^p</math> norm convergence follows in both cases for exactly those <math>\delta</math> where <math>(1-|\xi|^2)^{\delta}_+</math> is the [[Fourier multiplier|symbol]] of an <math>L^p</math> bounded [[Fourier multiplier]] operator.

For <math>n=2</math>, that question has been completely resolved, but for <math>n \geq 3</math>, it has only been partially answered.  The case of <math>n=1</math> is not interesting here as convergence follows for <math>p \in (1, \infty)</math> in the most difficult <math>\delta = 0</math> case as a consequence of the <math>L^p</math> boundedness of the [[Hilbert transform]] and an argument of [[Marcel Riesz]].

Define <math>\delta (p)</math>, the "critical index", as

:<math>\max( n|1/p - 1/2| - 1/2, 0)</math>.

Then the '''Bochner–Riesz conjecture''' states that

:<math>\delta > \delta (p)</math>

is the necessary and sufficient condition for a <math>L^p</math> bounded Fourier multiplier operator. It is known that the condition is necessary.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ciatti |first1=Paolo |last2=Gonzalez |first2=Eduardo |last3=Lanza de Cristoforis |first3=Massimo |last4=Leonardi |first4=Gian Paolo |title=Topics in Mathematical Analysis |contribution=Lectures on eigenfunctions of the Laplacian |contributor-last1=Sogge |contributor-first1=C. D. |date=2008 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=9789812811066 |page=347 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=u9glY7i6R2UC&pg=PA347 |language=en}}</ref>
